# A ball times a limb, two-limb center, finite core

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_scale_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, that contains $x a$ for every $x \in X$, with $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x a : x \in X \,\}.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_z = c_{z0} + c_{z1}$.

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet. The operations of the public headers call [`ball_scale_2_full`](ball_scale_2_full.md), which computes this kernel and then the fix-up of its results.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $c_x$ is normalized: $c_{x0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{x0} + c_{x1})$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $c_z$ is normalized: $c_{z0} = \mathrm{RN}(c_{z0} + c_{z1})$.
- $\lvert (x a) - c_z\rvert \le r_z$ for all real $x$ with $\lvert x - c_x\rvert \le r_x$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_scale_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/Ball2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/Ball2.v), against `ball_scale_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); `make -C proofs` finds no axiom in its proof beyond the four allowed ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition ball_scale_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (2 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall cx0 cx1 rx a : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec cx0 cx1 ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  0 <= rx ->
  let '(cz0, cz1, rz) := ball_scale_2 emin prec tie_even cx0 cx1 rx a in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  normalized_2 emin prec cz0 cz1 /\
  (forall x : R, Rabs (x - (cx0 + cx1)) <= rx -> Rabs ((x * a) - (cz0 + cz1)) <= rz).
```

## Source

**Algorithm:** midpoint-radius scaling (Milestone 1 listing, second radius design). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_scale_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_scale_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_2_1`](mul_2_1.md).

```
# A ball times a number a of the format, with a 2-limb center: the center by mul_2_1, the radius in the second design.
# The radius is evaluated by operations rounded to nearest on nonnegative values and inflated
# once (milestone1.md, "The radius, second design"): E turns the error bound of the center
# kernel mul_2_1 into a multiple of |cz0|, G covers the roundings of the radius, H what underflow
# loses and the absolute term of the bound. Each is an exact expression rounded up. H also
# contains eta/(2u), the smallest normal number, which no bound needs: it makes H, and with it
# every radius a kernel returns, a normal number, because a fused operation with a subnormal
# operand is slow on some processors (decisions.md, the log of 2026-11-19).

(cz0, cz1)  = mul_2_1(cx0, cx1, a)
aa          = abs(a)
az          = abs(cz0)
p           = prod(aa, rx)
t           = fma(az, const up(unit(mul_2_1)/(1-unit(mul_2_1))*(1+u)), p)
rz          = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+tiny(mul_2_1)/(1-unit(mul_2_1))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#ball_scale_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | smallest slack of the radius, in gaps |
|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 87 612 192 | 0 | 1.375 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 60 runners on 3 machines | 85 079 340 | 0 | 1.37500 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 843 994 | 0 | 1.375 (`fp:3:-6:2`) |

The slack is how far the returned radius is above the smallest radius that encloses the exact set, in units in the last place of the radius: below 1, a radius one unit smaller would not enclose it.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: [`ball_scale_2_full`](ball_scale_2_full.md) states that ([What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values) says what the library does now).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
